text: To Whom It May Concern, On XX/XX/2023 I logged into my XXXX XXXX XXXX XXXX issued by Wells Fargo bank and noticed I had been assessed a late fee of USD {$25.00} as well as an interest fee of USD {$48.00}. This was surprising as I have had no record of late fees on this account and thought I had paid off the balance in full for the prior statements. I then called Wells Fargo on the same day and was informed by a representative that I had been charged both fees as there was a balance of USD {$180.00} that had been left unpaid on my XXXX statement. Looking into the charges, I realized that my building had added those charges without my knowledge, given the card in question is linked to my building to pay for rent and utilities. In light of the unexpected charge and my lack of late payments prior, I requested that both the late fee and interest charges be refunded. The representative informed me that unfortunately only the late fee could be refunded and that the interest fee would not be removed. This seems particularly unreasonable, given Wells Fargo bank assessed the interest payment on the entire outstanding balance of my card at the time, totaling USD {$4300.00}, rather than only on the USD {$180.00} that was overdue. When I pointed this out to the representative, they sought a supervisor, who unfortunately upheld the original decision not to refund any of the assessed interest charge. This not only feels unreasonable punitive, but also markedly unfair given other financial institutions routinely refund assessed interest for first infractions on request. Even if Wells Fargo chooses not to follow this industry standard, I would think that it would be reasonable to only charge interest on the actual amount overdue vs. the much larger standing balance, the vast majority of which was not in overdue status.

It requires debt collectors to follow certain procedures when communicating with consumers about debt collection : Validation notice Within five days of the initial communication, debt collectors must send consumers a written notice that includes the amount of the debt, the creditor 's name, and a statement that the debt will be considered valid if the consumer doesn't dispute it within 30 days. The notice must also state that the debt collector will provide the consumer with the original creditor 's name and address if requested within 30 days. Disputed debts If the consumer disputes the debt, the debt collector must stop collection efforts and : Obtain verification of the debt or a copy of a judgment Mail the verification or judgment to the consumer Other provisions Debt collectors are also prohibited from taking certain actions, such as : Threatening or taking non-judicial action to disable or dispossess property if there is no right to possession, no intention to take possession, or the property is exempt by law Using unfair or unconscionable means to collect a debt, such as collecting amounts that aren't authorized by the agreement creating the debt or permitted by law

label: debt-collection
text: I am writing to formally lodge a complaint against Midland Credit Management ( MCM ), a debt collection agency that has been reporting an alleged debt on my credit report. MCM has repeatedly violated my rights as a consumer under the Fair Debt Collection Practices Act ( FDCPA ) and the Fair Credit Reporting Act ( FCRA ) by failing to validate this debt and continuing collection efforts despite my formal requests to cease and desist. Here are the details of my complaint : 1. Failure to Validate Debt : After receiving notification from MCM about an alleged debt, I promptly requested validation of this debt in accordance with my rights under the FDCPA. MCM has failed to provide any verifiable information to substantiate the validity of this debt. The provided a single bill. Despite their failure to validate the debt, MCM continues to report it to the credit bureaus, damaging my credit report and financial standing. 2. Continued Requests for Information Without Verification : Despite their inability to validate the debt, MCM continues to request personal information from me. This repeated demand for information, without any substantiation of the debt, constitutes a further violation of my rights under the FDCPA. 3. Continued Collection Efforts After Cease and Desist : Also, on one of our many calls I requested a formal cease and desist letter to MCM, instructing them to stop all communication and collection efforts regarding this alleged debt. Despite my request, I continue to receive mail and collection notices from MCM. This ongoing communication is a clear violation of the FDCPA and my rights as a consumer. 4. Impact on Credit Report : The continued reporting of this unverifiable debt on my credit report has caused significant damage to my credit score and has hindered my ability to secure favorable financial terms. I believe this is a violation of the FCRA, as MCM has failed to ensure the accuracy of the information they are reporting.

text: After reviewing my credit report, I noticed this company has been illegally reporting information to credit bureaus without my consent ( Credit Utilization ). This is an invasion of my privacy and against the law. 15 U.S. Code 1681- Congressional findings and statement of purpose ( a ) Accuracy and fairness of credit reporting The Congress makes the following findings : ( 1 ) The banking system is dependent upon fair and accurate credit reporting. Inaccurate credit reports directly impair the efficiency of the banking system, and unfair credit reporting methods undermine the public confidence which is essential to the continued functioning of the banking system. ( 2 ) An elaborate mechanism has been developed for investigating and evaluating the credit worthiness, credit standing, credit capacity, character, and general reputation of consumers. ( 3 ) Consumer reporting agencies have assumed a vital role in assembling and evaluating consumer credit and other information on consumers. ( 4 ) There is a need to insure that consumer reporting agencies exercise their grave responsibilities with fairness, impartiality, and a respect for the consumers right to privacy. ( b ) Reasonable procedures It is the purpose of this subchapter to require that consumer reporting agencies adopt reasonable procedures for meeting the needs of commerce for consumer credit, personnel, insurance, and other information in a manner which is fair and equitable to the consumer, with regard to the confidentiality, accuracy, relevancy, and proper utilization of such information in accordance with the requirements of this subchapter.

text: Regarding my Apple Card from Goldman Sachs, I have had this card for years and have built up my credit limit. Its my primary credit card. I added my partner to the card as a co-owner years ago. text: Under Title 12 CFR 1026.10 ( a ) ( 3 ), part of the Truth in Lending Act ( TILA ), creditors are mandated to promptly credit consumer accounts for payments or other transactions. If a creditor fails to credit a consumers account, it constitutes a significant billing error. This provision ensures that consumers are accurately charged and that payments are correctly applied to their accounts. When a creditor fails to credit a payment, it not only impacts the consumer 's financial standing but also may lead to wrongful late fees, damage to credit scores, and undue stress. Under this regulation, consumers have the right to dispute such errors and seek corrections. The creditor is obligated to investigate and resolve the issue, including crediting the account with the proper amount and rectifying any related adverse effects. This regulation protects consumer rights and ensures financial integrity in billing practices Under 12 CFR 1026.13, creditors must address billing errors promptly. Sections ( 1 ) through ( 7 ) outline the process : XXXX XXXX : Creditors must investigate disputes and resolve them within specific timeframes. XXXX XXXX : Consumers must receive written acknowledgment of their dispute within XXXX days. Correction : Errors must be corrected, including adjustments to account balances and refunds if applicable. Notice of XXXX : Creditors must notify consumers of the resolution outcome. Error Explanation : If an error isnt found, a clear explanation must be provided. Interim Credit : XXXX credits XXXX be required while disputes are investigated. Continued Charges : Consumers should not be liable for disputed amounts while the investigation is ongoing. These regulations ensure fair treatment and accurate billing for consumers..
